line: Crowley on the Queens: the letter Hé of the Name, the Mother of the series, and the Queen of Cups (pdf p21, p24, p139, p151, p261).

sections.title: The letter of the Name
sections.line: Crowley on the Queens as the letter Hé of the Name, and on the Court cards as a pictorial analysis of the four letters and the four Elements (pdf p139).

quotes.quote: The Queens represent the letter Hé of the Name.
These cards constitute a pictorial analysis of the powers of the four letters of the Name and the four Elements.

sections.title: Mother in the series
sections.line: Crowley on the terms Knight, Queen, Prince and Princess for the series Father, Mother, Son, Daughter (pdf p24), on the Court cards referred to the numbers 2, 3, 6 and 10 (pdf p261), and on the Hebrew system (pdf p24).

quotes.quote: It has been thought better, for the present pack, to adopt the term “Knight”, “Queen”, “Prince” and “Princess”, to represent the series Father, Mother, Son, Daughter, because the doctrine involved, which is extraordinarily complex and difficult, demands it.
The Court cards are referred to the numbers 2, 3, 6 and 10
The Hebrew system is straightforward and irreversible; it postulates Father and Mother from whose union issue Son and Daughter.

sections.title: Hé and the Queen of Cups
sections.line: Crowley on the letter traditionally consecrated to the Great Mother (pdf p21) and on the Queen of Cups as the watery part of Water (pdf p151).

quotes.quote: This is the letter traditionally consecrated to the Great Mother.
The Queen of Cups represents the watery part of Water, its power of reception and reflection.
